title: On-prem CUDA memory leak & retry-policy investigation - Novum Health POC
summary: Deep-dive into recurring OOMs and intermittent CUDA timeouts on Novum's on-prem POC cluster. Discussed likely memory leak patterns in KV cache + batching interaction, retry semantics, driver/version mismatches, and mitigating configs (batch caps, quantization profiles, periodic cache eviction). Agreed next steps: collect full nvidia-smi/dmesg traces, reproduce with a controlled workload, run memory-heavy stress test with debug build, and try 2 kernel/driver combinations. Priority: reduce production OOM risk and define safe retry/backoff policy.
next_steps: SE to upload debug-run checklist and log collection script to shared folder - due 2026-03-12
Customer to run controlled repro and share logs (nvidia-smi, dmesg, runtime logs) - target 2026-03-13
Schedule kernel/driver matrix test with Redwood infra - tentatively 2026-03-16

transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-09
- Start: 15:02 UTC
- Duration: 58m
- Attendees: Ethan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Carlos (Redwood SRE), Daniel (Novum ML Infra), Leila (Novum Platform), Marcus (Novum CTO), Sana (DevOps), Oliver (Security)

Auto-summary (may be imperfect): Investigate OOMs on on-prem POC. Suspect kv cache growth combined with burst batching leads to CUDA OOMs; sometimes GPU driver TDR/timeout reported. Discussed retry semantics: current client retries are blind and can amplify OOMs. Agreed to safe caps and logs.

[00:00] Ethan: Okay everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Daniel: Hi all, Daniel here. Were the infra lead, been chasing these OOMs for two weeks.
[00:12] Leila: Leila from platform, hi.
[00:15] Marcus: Marcus, CTO.
[00:18] Priya: Priya, SE at Redwood. Ill lead the debug steps.
[00:22] Carlos: Carlos, Redwood SRE - looking at driver/host level.
[00:26] Sana: Sana - DevOps, Im owning the onprem cluster.
[00:29] Oliver: Oliver - security / compliance.

[02:02] Ethan: Goal for today: get to root cause (or shortlist) and agree next steps so you can avoid production impact. Daniel, can you summarize the symptoms again?
[02:12] Daniel: Yeah. The cluster is a 4-node A40-ish equivalent setup, running our POC. Intermittent OOMs during long-chat workloads and heavy batch infer. Error logs show "CUDA out of memory" then a few minutes later the node drops to kernel OOM or driver reports TDR timeouts. Sometimes process restarts automatically, other times whole gpu state is lost and K8s evicts pods.

[04:05] Priya: When you say long-chat, what sequence lengths and batch sizes?
[04:12] Daniel: Sequence up to 4k tokens in repro, and batch sizes burst to 24 for a short window. Typically we had continuous prefix caching enabled.

[05:00] Priya: That combination is risky: long KV cache growth plus sudden large batch can exhaust device memory even if avg token rate is low. Weve seen leaks where cache isn't trimmed on rollout changes or quantization promotes temporary allocations.

[06:20] Carlos: Also driver TDRs often point to GPU kernel hang rather than purely allocation. Could be an instruction path hitting a slow kernel on that driver build. What driver version are you on?
[06:28] Sana: Were on 470.something enterprise driver; a handful of nodes show 470.161, others 470.129, we suspected drift.

[07:05] Priya: Version drift is red flag. Some runtime kernels behave badly across minor driver differences and cuda-toolkit mismatches.

[08:10] Marcus: Is this likely a Redwood runtime bug or our infra mismatch? Need a quick call on ownership.
[08:18] Ethan: Short answer: could be both. Well try to isolate with a minimal repro and matrix tests. Redwood will provide guidance and config guards; Novum runs repros and share logs.

[09:30] Daniel: We captured one crash dump - it references a kernel launch failure in "attention_cuda.cu" (transcribed name, raw logs attached). Could the KV cache implementation cause many small allocations?
[09:44] Priya: KV cache is pre-allocated usually, but in some quantized paths we use staging buffers and small temp allocations for dequantize/compress steps. If those spill over due to a large batch, the runtime will try to allocate and OS/GPU can fail. Also if we have continuous prefix caching forever it will grow unless we cap entries.

[11:00] Leila: Our current policy is infinite prefix cache for the POC to maximize responsiveness.
[11:07] Priya: That needs a cap. Suggestion: implement LRU eviction by token count and a max cache memory cap per-device. Also add a cap on concurrent batch tokens that the endpoint will accept - circuit-breaker style.

[13:20] Carlos: On the driver side, the TDR suggests kernel hang; two possibilities: faulty kernel path or a slow kernel that trips watchdog. You can try raising the TDR timeout (Windows-specific usually) or on Linux check nvidia-smi persist mode and nv-hostengine behavior.

[14:10] Sana: This is Linux. We saw messages like "NVRM: Xid (PCIe) 79" in dmesg around the time of crashes.

[14:25] Priya: Xid 79 often hints at GPU fault from illegal memory access, but exact meaning varies by driver. Important we collect full dmesg + kernel oops.

[16:00] Daniel: When the pod restarts, our client does immediate retries and that creates another burst and worsens the OOMs. The retry backoff is naive.

[16:18] Ethan: Right — blind retries can amplify resource contention. We recommend idempotent retry semantics with exponential backoff and jitter, and server-side throttling with 429/Retry-After when we detect memory pressure.

[17:02] Priya: Redwood runtime supports backpressure signals: you can set a max inflight token or generate 429s on queue depth exceed. But if the client ignores 429s you still get retries. So client-side change needed too.

[18:40] Marcus: What about quantization? Could an 8-bit path blow memory?
[18:48] Priya: Quantization reduces model weights memory but sometimes requires decompression buffers during inference for fused kernels. Depending on kernel implementation you can end up with temporary peak allocations that exceed the savings. We saw a case where int8 path used a staging float buffer equal to half model size momentarily.

[20:00] Carlos: We should try a test matrix: full-precision vs int8; batch sizes 1/8/16/24; prefix cache on/off; driver versions 470.129/470.161 and maybe 510 series. That will help separate allocation vs kernel-hang issues.

[22:10] Sana: We can run that but need a test harness. Can Redwood share a script?

[22:18] Priya: Yes. I upload a script that drives steady-state token streams and also bursts. Will include nvidia-smi snapshots every second and heap profile toggles. Link will go to shared folder: https://redwood.example/shared/novum/oom-debug (placeholder)

[24:05] Daniel: Also, how do we ensure we don't lose data or PII during logs? Oliver - any concerns?
[24:12] Oliver: We need logs scrubbed before transfer, no raw patient data. We'll provide sanitized identifiers; Redwood can sign an NDA addendum if needed.

[25:40] Ethan: Back to retry semantics — two levels: client retries and server retry policy. Implementing server side circuit breaker that returns 429 quickly when memory headroom low is best. Also recommend a per-model inflight token cap that when reached returns 503/429 and suggests fallback model.

[27:55] Priya: We'll propose default safe knobs: max_inflight_tokens=500k per-device, max_batch_size=12, cache_max_tokens=1M with LRU eviction. These are conservative; Novum can tune.

[29:10] Daniel: If we set these caps, will we see reduced throughput?
[29:17] Priya: Yes short-term throughput may drop on bursty workloads but reduces risk of catastrophic OOMs and node evictions. Also we can enable prefix caching eviction to maintain response latency for typical flows.

[31:00] Marcus: Are there visibility tools we can enable to see cache growth over time?
[31:05] Priya: Redwood Console exposes token-level cache usage, per-route latency and memory estimates; we'll give you a dashboard and alerts.

[33:20] Carlos: Important to get driver/kernel matrix. A lot of odd Xid codes correspond to kernel bugs fixed in a later driver. If the repro fails on one driver but not another that's telling.

[35:10] Daniel: We did a test where one node was 470.161 and another 470.129 and the 161 node crashed more often.

[35:25] Priya: Interesting. Could be that 470.161 introduced a new kernel that interacts badly with a fused attention kernel. We'll include kernel-specific build flags in our debug build.

[37:45] Sana: On the K8s side, pods are getting OOMKilled after GPU fails; do you recommend different pod restartPolicy?
[37:54] Carlos: If GPU state is corrupted, restarting the pod won't help unless the driver recovers. We recommend node-level fencing: when NVRM Xid occurs, cordon node and run recovery steps. Also set pod disruption budgets carefully.

[39:12] Priya: For short term, add health-check that queries runtime memory headroom and failfast with a 429 to client rather than letting retry loops occur.

[41:00] Daniel: Regarding logs, what exact artifacts do you need?
[41:06] Priya: Full dmesg, /var/log/messages around crash, nvidia-smi -q snapshots every 1s for the period, runtime logs with DEBUG traces, a core dump if possible, and the exact model/config used. Also the workload driver that produced burst.

[42:30] Ethan: We'll prepare a checklist: log types, commands, and how to sanitize. We'll post doc and script to shared folder.

[44:10] Marcus: Any quick mitigations we can enable now?
[44:16] Priya: 1) Reduce max_batch_size to 12, 2) enable cache eviction policy (limit total tokens), 3) set client backoff to exponential with jitter up to 30s, 4) pin driver to the more stable version if matrix shows differences, 5) enable conservative fallback model for bursts.

[46:20] Daniel: About fallback model: can Redwood route to a CPU-based cheaper model automatically when GPU memory low?
[46:28] Priya: Yes. Smart routing can fallback to a smaller model or even a CPU path. That avoids OOM while returning slightly lower quality. We'll help configure policies.

[48:02] Sana: Let's talk about quantization-specific tests: do we need to test both fused/unfused kernels?
[48:10] Priya: Yes. Try both fused kernels (faster but riskier) and dequantize-staging path. Also test with cache disabled to remove that variable.

[50:00] Oliver: From security side, we need to ensure any debug snapshots don't leak keys. Keep KMS logs out.

[51:12] Ethan: Noted. We'll share sanitized guidance and a signed addendum if needed.

[52:40] Priya: Ok to recap: Redwood to share script + debug flags + default conservative knobs; Novum to run repro and upload logs; both to run driver/kernel matrix and report back; set temporary caps and client backoff; cordon node on Xid events as precaution.

[54:10] Daniel: Agree. One question: any ETA on code-level fix if it's a runtime bug?
[54:18] Priya: If reproduction shows a specific kernel/path bug we can triage quickly; a patch might take 2-4 weeks depending on complexity. But the operational knobs should mitigate risk immediately.

[55:00] Ethan: Great. Well send meeting notes and the shared links. Thanks everyone.
[55:10] Marcus: Thanks.
[55:15] Daniel: Thanks all.
